questions_for_review.detail: The block records status `early_close` at that instant, and the tool ships `early_close(1 * 3_600)`. On the 2022-05-30 sheet the outright Nikkei and BTIC Nikkei lines are merged under one label and the printed instant is the BTIC-style `1:00 (close)`; every other 2022 sheet prints a separate `Nikkei` row governed by the EQUITIES `12:00` halt, and the block's own verbatim calls the merge 'a residual ambiguity'. Ruling needed: ship `01:00`, or the EQUITIES `12:00`, or `Unsourced`?
questions_for_review.title: `globex_nikkei_225_dollar` on 2022-05-30: the printed close `01:00 CT` falls in the small hours of the trade date, before the ordinary day session begins at `08:30 CT`.
questions_for_review.tool_default: ship early_close(1 * 3_600) as the block states

questions_for_review.detail: `dairy`'s ordinary week is one wrapped leg per trade date, 17:00 CT the previous evening into a 16:00 CT close (13:55 CT on Fridays); `globex_grains`'s is 19:00 CT the previous evening into 07:45 CT, then the 08:30-13:20 CT day session whose close is the trading day's final closing phase, then the 14:30-16:00 CT post-close period. A family table holds one scalar boundary per trade date, so a folded group whose own session moves at a different instant cannot be represented by the crate family's row; the tool compares the two row by row on each group's own grid and ships the crate family's row.
questions_for_review.title: The `dairy` -> `globex_grains` fold joins two different clocks.
questions_for_review.tool_default: keep the fold for status only; the crate family's instants stand

questions_for_review.detail: `lumber`'s ordinary week is one flat Monday-Friday 09:00-15:05 CT session inside a single civil day, with a 06:00 CT pre-open; `globex_livestock`'s is one flat Monday-Friday 08:30-13:05 CT session inside a single civil day, with an 08:00-08:30 CT pre-open and a 14:30-16:00 CT post-close period. questions_for_review.detail: On these dates the crate family's own document states that the prior-evening leg did not run and the day session opened at 08:30 CT, so the tool ships a `LateOpen`; the folded group's own clock reopens at its ordinary evening open and states no row, so it treats the same trade date as ordinary. questions_for_review.detail: Every one is a `LateOpen` the crate family's own document states for the day after a closure (globex_grains 2022-07-05 (late open 08:30 CT); globex_grains 2023-07-05 (late open 08:30 CT); globex_grains 2023-12-26 (late open 08:30 CT); globex_grains 2024-01-02 (late open 08:30 CT); globex_grains 2024-07-05 (late open 08:30 CT); globex_grains 2024-12-26 (late open 08:30 CT)). The block carries one entry per holiday date, so the trade date that follows a closure has no entry of its own and the tool creates the row from the closure entry's printed open.
questions_for_review.title: 6 rows are keyed to trade dates the block has no entry for.

questions_for_review.detail: The 2024 Good Friday windows are the cause: the T2 service was read for 2024-03-28 .. 2024-03-30, so the Sunday 2024-03-31 reopen (and with it whether the trade date 2024-04-01 lost its prior-evening leg, which matters for `globex_grains`) is outside the document. The tool ships no row for 2024-04-01. Per group: dairy: 2023-11-23, 2023-11-24, 2024-03-29, 2024-11-28, 2024-11-29; globex_cryptocurrency: 2024-03-29; globex_energy: 2024-03-29, 2024-03-29; globex_equity_index: 2024-03-29; globex_fx: 2024-03-29; globex_grains: 2024-03-29; globex_interest_rates: 2024-03-29; globex_livestock: 2024-03-29; lumber: 2024-03-29.
questions_for_review.title: 14 closure entries print no reopen at all.
questions_for_review.tool_default: ship nothing for 2024-04-01 and record the gap

questions_for_review.detail: `holidays!` fails the build for a row with an empty document id, so an `Unsourced` row must name an artifact. The tool cites the saved T2 response that returns `hasEvents:false` for that window (CME-SVC-2023-01-15, CME-SVC-2023-02-19, CME-SVC-2023-04-06), which is the operator's own machine channel read as bytes. The alternative is to split the family's coverage into three windows and claim no window over those dates. Two consequences are deliberately left unsourced: the day *after* each of these three holidays (2023-01-17, 2023-02-21 and, for `globex_grains`, 2023-04-10) may have lost its prior-evening leg the way 2024-01-02 and 2023-12-26 did, and no document in the store states whether it did, so those trade dates ship no row and the crate reports the family's ordinary week there.
questions_for_review.title: The 3 uncovered 2023 dates cite the operator's own negative control as their document id.
questions_for_review.tool_default: cite the negative control, keep one 2022-2024 window

questions_for_review.detail: The T2 service returns only the ten representative products and no Nikkei is among them, so the 2024 Nikkei dates are inside the family's window but carry no operator statement. The rows clip nothing and keep the window contiguous. Ruling needed: confirm, or shrink this family's coverage to 2022-01-01..2023-12-31 and let 2024 be 'no answer'?
questions_for_review.title: `globex_nikkei_225_dollar` ships 16 `Unsourced` rows, 13 of them the whole 2024 window.
questions_for_review.tool_default: keep the contiguous window with `Unsourced` rows

questions_for_review.detail: The fix INDEX's section 2 rows (`CME-SVC-2023-01-15, CME-SVC-2023-02-19, CME-SVC-2023-04-06`) carry no `T1`/`T2` token in their description column; the file states the channel is `tier T2 under LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES` on line 14. unsourced_dates_from_missing_block.reason: 2023 Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day (Monday 16 January 2023) - ALL product groups (Equity Index, Nikkei, Interest Rates, FX, Energy, Metals, Grains, Livestock, Cryptocurrency, Dairy, Lumber). Channels tried: holiday-calendar/files/*.xls (only 2023-mlk-day-holiday-schedule-compact-mgex-dme.xls exists and it carries MGEX and DME rows only); trading-hours/files/mlk-day-2023.pdf and presidents-day-2023.pdf (live 404 via r.jina.ai); Wayback CDX prefix on cmegroup.com/trading-hours/files (re-counted 2026-09-12 from cdx_47e9ad.json: only six 2023 one-pagers return 200, all from Memorial Day onward - round 0 said seven); Wayback captures of /services/trading-hours-by-product for fromEventDate=2023-01-15 (the only 200 capture is 2024-07-08T16:14:38Z; re-read from those bytes on 2026-09-12 it carries hasEvents:false with all ten products' event arrays empty - saved as raw/cme-2022-2024-fix/neg_api_2023-01-15.json. This is a rolling-history limit, not a rule about past dates: the same crawl returns full events for fromEventDate=2023-12-24 and for every 2024 window); 2023-holiday-calendars.zip (404); archive.today (HTTP 429). The 16 Jan 2023 archived holiday-calendar page shows CME linking this holiday to trading-hours.html#foi=F&tradeDate=2023-01-16, a client-rendered view with no archived payload.

2023 Presidents Day (Monday 20 February 2023) - ALL product groups. Same channels and same outcome as 2023 MLK (presidents-day-2023.pdf was never crawled at all rather than crawled and 404, so its absence is weaker evidence than the mlk-day-2023 404; the T2 window is empty either way - raw/cme-2022-2024-fix/neg_api_2023-02-19.json); the trading-hours.html deep link is #foi=F&tradeDate=2023-02-20.

2023 Good Friday (Friday 7 April 2023) - ALL product groups. Same channels and same outcome (T2 window empty - raw/cme-2022-2024-fix/neg_api_2023-04-06.json); deep link #foi=F&tradeDate=2023-04-07. Note this is the year CME is understood to have run a limited Good Friday session around the employment report, so the gap is materially more than a repeat of the 2022 full closure and must not be filled by pattern.
